SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Observe the fleet without exporting its customers.

Entity and store dimensions explain movement; customer data stays out of telemetry.

Implemented lab

The synthetic container lab is validated. Technical extension points on this page remain proposals unless explicitly identified as implemented. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

Implemented container logging extension

The consolidated lab exports minimised JSON application logs through the OTel Collector to Loki and provisions Grafana at the local gateway path /grafana/. Traces still use a debug exporter; metrics backends and regional telemetry isolation remain pilot work. Run ./lab telemetry for the end-to-end gate. See the consolidated lab observability guide for exact configuration and execution limits.

Instrumentation contract

SignalDimensionsHandling
Policy evaluation spansSource store, destination store/entity, allowed resultNo raw OPA input, customer IDs, payload or grants in trace attributes.
Federation spansOwner store, recipient entity, policy generationRegional collectors in production; synthetic harness output locally.
Metrics to addQueue depth/age, export denials, OPA errors, purge lag, placement conflictsUse bounded entity/store dimensions; avoid customer cardinality.
AuditCustomer-specific decision and transfer receiptsSeparate durable regional evidence, not sampled tracing.

Implemented versus proposed

The harness uses the OpenTelemetry Python SDK, a local JSONL exporter and optional OTLP HTTP export to a Compose Collector. The real-container acceptance verified Collector span receipt and API-generated logs reaching Loki through the Collector with matching trace IDs in exported API spans; the provisioned Grafana dashboard is accessible through the gateway. Traces still use a debug exporter, not a searchable trace backend. Regional telemetry isolation remains pilot work. Prometheus dashboards, regional collectors and sanitised cross-region aggregation are extension tasks, not implemented services.

Global monitor boundary

The hosted monitor contains only synthetic data. Its map shows legal entity locations separately from physical stores. Animated paths illustrate recent acknowledged events; they are not packet capture or proof of geography. A production global dashboard should receive approved aggregates and keep customer investigations within authorised regional sessions.

Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Operational isolation decision: use three regional work classes: authority guard, operational delivery and bulk reconciliation. Separate relay paths, queues/topics, worker groups, connection/concurrency budgets and retry/quarantine paths. A policy transaction advances scoped authority and creates a guard intent plus one reconciliation cursor; it must not enumerate affected rows. Operational commits remain local ACID with outbox/audit/idempotency. Operational priority never bypasses current policy. Source restriction commit, remote enforcement and physical convergence are separate milestones. Read the Work isolation page before implementing any queue or policy change. The interactive lab and admission specification are synthetic; the v3 database harness still has its original process lock and serial worker.

Extend the v3 operational PoC, preserving 30 legal entities and three independent single-node store models. Business data is normalized across 12 tables; sovereignty policies live in parallel control tables. A separate party scope exports only id/global_party_id/party_type; relationship scopes export connected whitelisted graphs. Global distribution still needs grants and approved geography; deny overrides. Do not infer relationship access from a global party, common store or shared identity. Keep the single local transaction and asynchronous destination acknowledgement distinct. The hosted UI is a labelled browser simulation. The unified Docker/CockroachDB/OPA suite and live Chromium generator/migration walkthrough passed. Database crash boundaries, accessibility and pilot load remain separate gates. Use synthetic data only. Deliver bounded adapters, actual migrations, meaningful invariant tests and honest run results.

Apply the normalized operational extension before the earlier component requirements below.

Add low-cardinality metrics for owner-entity/store lag, policy failures and reconciliation milestones. Use regional collector gateways with redaction and approved export rules. Test accidental customer IDs in URLs, attributes and exception messages. Keep customer-linked audit out of unrestricted global dashboards.
